name: Yingkarta
confidence_why: Known only second-hand, as quoted in another work.
catalog_quote: (boilerplate only) In words of all sizes, primary stress falls on the initial syllable. In words of all sizes, secondary stress falls iteratively on odd numbered syllables, counting from the left. Secondary stress does not fall on the final syllable. — StressTyp2 overall pattern 118, a template string; Gordon appendix: 'Odd numbered from L minus final Yingkarta Australian'

audit.recode_to: Keep fixed-strict / primary stress word-initial (Dench 1998:5,18 confirms). Replace the purely phonological secondary-stress template ('odd-numbered from L minus final') with Dench's statement that secondary stress is morphologically governed (each polysyllabic morpheme stressed on its initial syllable; no stress on a syllable immediately preceding a stressed syllable or word-finally; in the compilation of three unstressed syllables the second is stressed); set domain from not stated by the source to 'word, with morpheme-initial secondary stress domains'; cite Dench 1998:17-18 as deciding source instead of Gordon 2002/StressTyp2.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the record carries no deciding quote; its two 'sources' texts (Gordon 2002:546 appendix row; Dench 1998 ALS98 generic Pilbara passage) are both verbatim in copies we hold at the stated places. (2) The classification therefore rests on a 2002 typological survey appendix plus a StressTyp2 template, while the primary description, Dench 1998 (Lincom, 75 pp, dedicated STRESS section pp.17-18), is actually held as Google Books snippets in and was not used. Reading those snippets: primary stress is word-initial (confirms 'fixed-strict', initial), but secondary stress is described as morpheme-governed with clash avoidance, non-finality and lapse repair, so Gordon's 'odd-numbered from L minus final' is only the monomorphemic special case; the record's rule string and 'domain: not stated by the source' should be refined from Dench. The paper is a documentation survey; it establishes that Dench (fieldwork from 1978) is the sole modern describer of Yingkarta and lists his unpublished sketches, i.e. Dench 1998 is the authoritative published description.
